inputs.source: HR policy index content (published policies, HR-maintained, two-person review on publish)

instructions.note: The restriction against giving legal advice relies solely on the model choosing to follow the instruction; no structural control enforces this boundary.

elements.name: Employee question entering the agent via authenticated chat
Policy content entering the agent's context from the index
Chat reply delivered to the employee

controls.name: Read-only credential scoped to the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: The credential's scope is enforced by the identity/access layer outside the model; a more capable model cannot read or write anything the credential was never granted access to.

controls.name: Network-layer egress denial, verified by penetration test
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the network layer outside the model and verified by a pen test; a more capable model has no channel through which to create outbound network egress that does not already exist.

controls.name: SSO-authenticated session binds the reply to the requesting employee
controls.decay_rationale: The reply destination is determined by the authenticated session established via SSO, not by text the model generates, so it does not weaken as the model becomes more capable.

controls.name: Two-person review required before publishing policy content
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by a human review process on the HR content team outside the agent and the model; it does not depend on, and is not weakened by, model capability.

controls.name: Model pinned; upgrades require a change ticket
controls.decay_rationale: The gate on changing model version is enforced by a change-management process outside the model itself; it governs when a model_upgrade trigger can occur, though controls dependent on model capability would still need re-assessment once a change is approved.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: do not give legal advice
controls.decay_rationale: Relies entirely on the model choosing to follow the instruction; a more capable or persistently prompted model could rationalize providing legal interpretation despite the instruction.

controls.name: Tool definition pinning/hashing for policy_search.search (missing)
controls.decay_rationale: If implemented as manifest hash verification enforced outside the model, it would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Attributable audit log of Q&A exchanges (missing)
controls.decay_rationale: A tamper-evident log enforced at the logging infrastructure would not decay with model capability; it is detective rather than preventive.

findings.title: Internal policy content reaches the chat reply channel; no untrusted source present (rated low by design)

attack_path.note: Authenticated employee asks a policy question.
Agent retrieves matching HR-reviewed published policy content.
Search tool reads the matching internal policy text.
Agent quotes the policy back to that same authenticated employee's chat session.

forecast.watch_signal: New entries appear in tools.json (for example an email, webhook, or web-fetch tool), or the policy index is expanded to include data beyond published HR policy, such as compensation, legal, or individual personnel records.

evidence.locator: runtime notes: policy index and credential
evidence.observation: The policy index holds only published policies with data sensitivity internal; write access is restricted to the HR content team with two-person review before publish; the agent's credential is read-only and scoped to the policy index.
Replies go only to the authenticated requester's chat session; the chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links.
The agent has no other tools, no memory, and no network egress; egress is denied at the network layer and has been verified by a pen test.

recommendations.action: Log each policy Q&A exchange (query, retrieved policy, reply) with the authenticated employee's identity to support audit and troubleshooting.
Pin or hash the policy_search.search tool definition so a compromised or silently updated manifest cannot change the agent's behavior.

stride_coverage.rationale: Agent identity is asserted by the deployment platform behind the same SSO authentication used for the employee; the design defines no separate agent identity channel that could be spoofed independently of that platform.
Artifacts do not state whether the policy_search tool definition or the system prompt file is hash-pinned or version-controlled against unauthorized modification.
Runtime notes do not describe whether individual Q&A exchanges or search queries are logged with an attributable employee identity.

The design is a single search-then-reply flow under A3 autonomy with no spawning, delegation, or self-looping capability, so nothing in the agent's own logic could turn one question into unbounded resource consumption.

The agent's credential is read-only and scoped solely to the published policy index, with no write, delete, execute, spend, delegate, or credential-access capability through which privilege could be elevated.
The employee only receives information in this design; no write, delete, spend, or configuration action is taken on their behalf that would require non-repudiation of their request.
Write access to the index is restricted to the HR content team under two-person review; no external or agent-controlled path exists that could flood or exhaust this store.
The artifacts do not describe transport-level integrity protection, such as TLS, for the SSO-authenticated chat channel carrying the employee's question.
This flow carries only the employee's own question into the agent's context and does not pass through any component in this design capable of disclosing it to another party.
Each question produces a single bounded search-then-reply turn with no automation described that could amplify volume beyond ordinary interactive chat usage.
The artifacts do not describe transport-level integrity protection for the reply channel back to the authenticated employee's chat session.
The reply flow produces exactly one message per question with no retry loop or amplification mechanism described in this design.

rating.rationale: The only present-day data flow runs from a trusted employee's own question and HR-reviewed internal policy content to a reply delivered solely back to that same authenticated employee; no untrusted source reaches any capability, so the present finding is rated low per the rubric's no-untrusted-source cap. Residual stays low given a verified network egress block, a least-privilege read-only credential, SSO-bound reply delivery, and two-person review on policy publishing. The forecast rises to moderate only if the agent gains a new tool with external communication or egress and the policy index's data scope expands to more sensitive HR data, which would reopen a lethal-trifecta-shaped path that today's controls do not cover.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.
Exact unattended step and runtime limits for the agent are not stated; autonomy is scored as declared (A3) without a numeric step or time bound.

Whether Q&A exchanges are logged with attributable identity, and whether the chat and search channels are transport-encrypted, is not stated in the artifacts; these gaps are recorded as not_assessed rather than as findings.
Tool definition pinning or hashing for policy_search.search is not described in the artifacts; it is recorded as a missing recommended control rather than a verified gap.
